chunks: And the Commander of the Faithful (peace be upon him) said in one of his sermons: O people!

Indeed, this world is the abode of annihilation, and the Hereafter is the abode of permanence. So take from your passage for your permanent abode, and do not tear your veils before the One from whom your secrets are not hidden. Take your hearts out of this world before your bodies are taken out of it, for you were enlivened in this world, but you were created for the Hereafter.

This world is but like poison - it is eaten by one who does not know it. Indeed, when a servant dies, the angels say: "What has he sent forth?" while the people say: "What has he left behind?" So send forth virtue that will be for you, and do not leave behind a burden that will be against you.

For indeed, the deprived one is he who is deprived of the good of his wealth, and the envied one is he whose scales become heavy with charities and good deeds, through which his resting place in Paradise is beautified, and his passage on the Path is sweetened.

key_terms.الصراط: The Path/Bridge (Sirat) - the bridge over Hell that all must cross on the Day of Judgment
key_terms.دار بقاء: Abode of permanence - the eternal Hereafter
key_terms.دار فناء: Abode of annihilation - the transient world that is destined to perish
key_terms.مقر: Permanent abode/dwelling - refers to the afterlife as the true destination
key_terms.ممر: Passage/thoroughfare - metaphor for the transient nature of worldly life
key_terms.موازين: Scales - the scales of justice used to weigh deeds on the Day of Judgment

ai.seo_question: What did Imam Ali say about the world being a temporary passage and the Hereafter being permanent?
ai.summary: In this sermon delivered during an assembly in Shawwal 367 AH, Imam Ali (AS) admonishes people about the transient nature of this world versus the permanence of the Hereafter. He urges the audience to prepare for their eternal abode through good deeds and charity, warning that at death the angels ask about deeds sent forward while people only ask about wealth left behind. The original audience would have understood this as a call to detach from worldly attachment and invest in the afterlife through acts of righteousness.

en.bilal-muhammad: Amir al-Mu’minin (as) said in one of his sermons: O people!

Surely, this world is the Abode of Annihilation, and the Hereafter is the Abode of Permanence, so take from your sojourn what will aid you in your lodging. There is no need to disclose your hidden matters to Him from whom you cannot hide your secrets, so take your hearts out of this world before your body is taken out of it. You were enlivened for this world, but you were created for the Hereafter.

Surely, this world is like poison: it is eaten by one who knows not what it is. When a servant dies, the angels say: “What has he brought?”, while the people say: “what has he left behind?” Send virtues before you so that they may be for you, and do not leave anything that may be against you.

Surely, the deprived is one who is deprived of the goodness of his wealth, who will be envious of one whose scales become heavy with charity and good actions, through which his residence in Paradise is beautified and his trek on the Path is sweetened.
